title: Distinct HT partitioned on group hash
reasons: no visible template faster beyond its noise (best: q16 -7.4%; needs at least -7.9%)
summary:
I fixed both review points; the tree builds. The q16 gain is real but noisy: -10.9%, -9.8%, -3.3% and +0.2% across four runs.

What changed since the rejected version:

1. **Only the top 4 radix bits come from the group hash.** The distinct hash table now takes bits [44,48) from hash(main groups) instead of all 12. The lower radix bits still come from the full hash(G,x), so repartitioning can still split a heavy group. The stored hash is used consistently, so correctness is unchanged.
2. **New runtime memory gate.** `RadixPartitionedHashTable::EnablePartitionPrefix(GlobalSinkState&, idx_t)` is called from the `HashAggregateGlobalSinkState` constructor with the child's row estimate. Prefix mode turns on only when estimated rows × (row width + 16) ≤ query memory limit / 16. The existing plan-time setup is kept: grouped aggregates with estimated output ≥ 4096 that have distinct tables. Ungrouped DISTINCT never turns it on.

**Spill check with one dominant group** (90% of rows in one group, 40M distinct x, about 5000 groups, 8 threads, `memory_limit=500MB`):
- Baseline (feature disabled): 6.42 s.
- Previous 12-bit version: failed with Out of Memory.
- 4-bit version without the gate: OOM. A 2-bit version without the gate passed but took 10.5–11.3 s (+65%), which is what led to the gate.
- Final version: 6.55 s, because the gate turns the feature off. Results match.

**In-memory checks, no memory limit:**
- 4M rows with 90% in the NULL group: 498–543 ms baseline vs 543–573 ms mine, about +7%. This is the remaining cost on an adversarial case.
- 8M rows spread evenly over 5000 groups: 904 ms baseline vs 801 ms mine, -11%.

**q16:** the best version measured between 174 and 195 ms; mine measured 164–182 ms.

**Full bench:** geomean -0.1%. Nothing outside ±5%: q18 and q19 were +4.3%, q02 -4.1%.
notes:
- The q16 gain is very noisy on this tree: my build is steady at 164–182 ms, while the best version swings between 174 and 195 ms. Per run: -10.9, -3.3, -9.8, +0.2%.
- Taking all 12 radix bits from the group hash makes a dominant group OOM under a low memory limit. Even 2 bits without a memory gate was 65% slower in the spill case.
- I could not run the baseline binary directly. Baseline numbers came from rebuilding with the plan gate forced off (`if (false && ...)`), which gives the original code path; that change is reverted in the final tree.
- Possible follow-up: choose the number of prefix bits from the final radix bits, or measure skew from HLL or a partition histogram before combining. Either would need a global decision before any rows are sunk, because all threads must hash the same way.
